newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher ahead of rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher ahead of rate decision.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed slightly higher on Thursday as the market awaited the Bank of Israel's decision on interest rates, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.05 pct to 105.51
Volume including Makams was 129 million shekels.

"The market is waiting for the publication of (the June) interest rate and also to see what economic steps the government will take and if there will be any further cuts in the budget," said Miron Katzap, an analyst at Ilanot Batucha Investment House.

The Bank of Israel will publish its key lending rate for June on May 26. The central bank last cut interest rates, to 13.9 percent, at the end of February. Katzap said he expected that next week they would be lowered by 0.3 percentage point.

The Treasury has proposed a plan to reduce the 1997 budget by 700 million-800 million shekels, but Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Finance Minister Dan Meridor on Wednesday failed again to reach an agreement on the matter. The cabinet is due to be presented with a plan on May 30.

"There was balance in CPI-linked trading, with no bonds rising or falling sharply as we saw in the last couple of days," Katzap said. "Traders prefer unlinked bonds because of April's low consumer price index. But there are already fears in the market that the next CPI will be high as a correction to the low one."
April's 0.7 percent CPI rise was well below analysts' forecasts of about 1.1 percent.
Katzap said yields on CPI-linked bonds had stabilised at around four percent.

"Before the (April) CPI these yields were on their way down," he said. "Now they are stable at four percent. In the coming months, however, they will go below the four percent because the government is issuing fewer of these bonds."

Prices of dollar-linked bonds were higher because of a strengthening of the dollar worldwide, traders said. The shekel representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3960 shekels against 3.3880 on Wednesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
